newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil deputies vote on five telecom amendments.
newsitem.headline: Brazil deputies vote on five telecom amendments.

text.p: The Brazilian Chamber of Deputies approved four government-backed amendments to a new telecommunications bill and rejected another which was floated by the opposition and sought to keep rates under state control.
The lower house, which earlier Wednesday approved the bill itself, was due to continue voting on further amendments either later in the day or next week, congressional officials said.
Among those amendments was a proposal to limit foreign capital in Brazilian telecommunications companies.
The defeat of the opposition amendment Wednesday means private companies will be free to set their own rates three years after beginning operations.

One of the four government-backed amendments approved will prevent groups who win a telecommunications concession from also providing other services, like cable television, in the same area, said an aide to the bill's author Deputy Alberto Goldman.
The other three amendments which were approved referred to rules for a new sector regulator.
The General Telecommunications Law seeks to regulate Brazil's telecommunications sector and set down rules for the privatization of the federally owned Telebras.
Once the amendments have been approved, the bill advances to the Senate.
